text:
incident-bot: Alert: reserved-pool "resv-prod-eu-west-1" GPU utilization at 98% (5m avg). Queue growth observed for reserved tenants. Auto-scale attempted 3 times, hit scale ceiling. Pager routed to oncall.
emily: i'm on it, thanks. seeing large enqueue for reserved tenants — starting triage.
luca: logs show autoscaler failing with 429 from cloud API at the time of scale attempts. might be rate-limited by provider.
dan: confirmed, cloud API returned quota_exceeded at 2026-03-15T01:12:03Z for instance create. autoscaler retried and backed off.
emily: which tenants impacted? any enterprise customers in the pool?
ops-bot: Reserved pool allocation snapshot:
```
resv-prod-eu-west-1: total_gpus=128 reserved_alloc=120 used=118 free=10
active_queues: ArborBank=42, devx=3, internal=2, experimental=0
throttled_requests=5400/min
```
emily: ArborBank is the big one — their reserved jobs queued up. they're seeing 5xx and throttles reported by downstream.
marcus: i'll open bridge with their account team and notify them. @customer-ops please prep the customer-facing note.
customer-ops: on it, drafting: "We’re investigating elevated latency and throttling for reserved capacity in eu-west. Our on-call is working on mitigation."
luca: quick root cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor session(s) from one ArborBank workload holding GPUs longer than expected + autoscaler blocked by cloud rate limits. combined -> queue growth -> throttling fallback.
emily: can we identify noisy sessions? dan do we have per-session GPU time breakdown?
dan: pulling session logs — give me 30s.
dan: snippet:
```
2026-03-15T01:09:22Z arbor-job-987 start seq_len=4096 tokens
2026-03-15T01:09:23Z arbor-job-988 start seq_len=10240 tokens
2026-03-15T01:10:01Z arbor-job-988 still running (KV hits=12M)
```
emily: wow job-988 is huge seq_len 10k, maybe long context eval loop. that would hog the device.
luca: if we can preempt that session we free GPUs for smaller, latency-sensitive jobs. but need customer consent for preemption on reserved.
emily: agreed. Marcus / customer-ops coordinate with ArborBank for immediate mitigation: either pause that job or let us preempt under emergency.
marcus: pinged ArborBank PBX and sent email. they replied: "we're running a nightly backfill job — can pause — give us 10-15 mins to checkpoint." they asked if routing fallback available meantime.
emily: okay. mitigation plan:
1) enable temporary overflow routing for ArborBank to hosted fallback model for low-priority requests (non-SLA).
2) if ArborBank pauses the long job, SRE will evict session-988 after confirmation.
3) request manual bump of pool by +8 GPUs if provider quota allows; otherwise reassign capacity from non-prod.
luca: executing 1) now — adding routing rule to route requests with tag `priority:low` for ArborBank to hosted model `redwood-hosted/gptx-medium`.
ops-bot: Routing change applied: arborbank_low_priority -> redwood-hosted/gptx-medium (effective immediately).
emily: that should reduce queue ingress for latency users. dan, can you start graceful drain/preempt plan for session-988 after Marcus confirms?
dan: prepping evict script. will try a graceful checkpoint then kill. command I'm planning:
```
./evict_session --session-id arbor-job-988 --grace-period 60 --checkpoint=true
```
marcus: arbor responded: "pause confirmed for job-988, checkpoint in progress, ETA 8 mins. proceed with overflow routing." they asked for ETA to clear queue.
emily: estimate: with overflow routing + pause, queue should drop to normal in ~6-10 mins. but autoscaler still stuck — we should escalate to infra to request emergency manual scale if needed.
luca: i filed a provider support ticket: "quota_exceeded during autoscale attempts" ticket# 2026-AR-443. provider support ETA 45 mins. i'll also attempt manual instance create but may fail due to same quota.
emily: do manual scale attempt now, if it succeeds we can add +4 GPUs and reduce pressure.
dan: attempting manual create: `cloudctl compute instances create --pool resv-prod-eu-west-1 --count 4` -> 429 quota_exceeded.
ops-bot: manual scale failed with 429. provider recommends request increase via console; immediate scaling blocked.
emily: not ideal. prioritize eviction then. what's queue length now?
ops-bot: queue length (reserved-only): 180 -> 70 (after routing change).
emily: good. keep monitoring per-minute.
luca: monitoring p50 token latency for ArborBank: 180ms -> 2.1s peak -> now 450ms.
marcus: ArborBank on bridge: "we paused the backfill and checkpointed. thanks. We're seeing 200s timeouts to our app but retrying." they want an ETA for full recovery.
emily: tell them 10-15 mins unless cloud quota blocks further scaling. we'll follow up in 10.
customer-ops: message sent: "Thanks — we're seeing improvement. We'll confirm when normal throughput resumes."
dan: checkpoint finished, safe to preempt. executing evict script.
ops-bot: evict_session arbor-job-988 -> success. freed 1 GPU session.
ops-bot: pool used=117 free=11 queue=45 throttled_requests=1200/min
emily: nice. continue evict of other long-running sessions where safe. dan list top 5 longest:
dan: top long sessions:
- arbor-job-992 (seq_len=8192) running 18m
- arbor-job-995 (seq_len=6144) running 9m
- internal-eval-21 (seq_len=2048) running 4m
- devx-sim-77 (seq_len=10240) running 2m

will target arbor-job-992 after confirmation.
emily: Marcus confirm with ArborBank which of these are critical.
marcus: ArborBank flagged 992 as also backfill — okay to pause. 995 is live user test — keep.
ops-bot: evict arbor-job-992 -> success. freed 2 GPUs.
ops-bot: pool used=115 free=13 queue=22 throttled_requests=300/min
luca: autoscaler still in backoff state; it won't attempt new scales until cool-down 10m. given provider limit, manual scale is blocked. we should keep routing spillover and evictions until ticket resolved.
emily: Agreed. switch to containment mode. Actions recap:
- Routing overflow applied for low-priority (done)
- Evicted/backfilled long sessions (done x2)
- Manual scale attempted (blocked)
- Provider ticket open (ticket# 2026-AR-443)

Next: create incident bridge, notify oncall rotation for postmortem.
emily: @oncall-rotation can you take ownership for the followup timeline and postmortem? we need RCA on autoscaler backoff + provider quota + customer workload patterns.
oncall-rotation: taking ownership. I'll schedule a 1hr follow-up and add to triage board.
marcus: ArborBank status: "service degraded but routing mitigated most latency-sensitive traffic. we'll run a smaller backfill window tomorrow." they asked if we can recommend safeguards.
emily: recommend queue_limits and per-tenant concurrent session cap for reserved tenants, and a soft-eviction policy for long seq_len jobs. add to ops playbook.
luca: adding playbook item: per-tenant session cap, long-session detection (seq_len > 8k) -> auto-queue to non-reserved or require approval.
customer-ops: customer note: "Immediate mitigation applied. SRE evacuated long-running jobs and enabled overflow routing. Team will implement scheduling safeguards."
emily: marking incident P1 -> contained. creating incident ticket for postmortem and action items.
ops-bot: Incident bridge created: https://redwood/bridges/4999995678
emily: thanks everyone. I'll leave the channel open for anyone joining from infra/provider until ticket resolves. we will follow up with ArborBank and close once queue and throttles stable for 1h.
marcus: PATCH to ArborBank: "Thanks — we'll follow up tomorrow with proposed tenant-level limits and an ops schedule." :thumbsup:
luca: logging governance action: add quota-guard monitoring to alert earlier when provider responses 429 spike. file (#infra-guard-129).
oncall-rotation: follow-up meeting scheduled in 45m. assigning notes owner.
emily: closing realtime actions. status: contained -> monitoring. next updates in 10m or on change.
